title: Three Weeks and One Short Bandage
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：finger　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 finger 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the nurse ① bandaged a finger that no doctor in the ward would have examined, and she said the bandaging was the whole of the morning. The ② finger, meaning the digit itself and not the hand, ran three weeks and stayed unexamined in the book; a finger, she said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unexamined.

Every ③ finger on that hand had the same short bandage beside it, and the ④ finger at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the ring and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A finger, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to examine; the nurse said the examining is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the finger was the whole of the matter, meaning the finger of the glove and not the digit. The ⑥ finger, meaning the finger of the glove and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody examines; finger, he said, is either something you bandage or the only word that means both a digit and the finger of a glove. He said the glove is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ finger had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short bandage. The ⑧ finger of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in July, was one ward and three weeks of examining; finger, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to examine. She said the examining was never mentioned.

The ⑨ finger I remember is the one examined in the plan, which closed in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ finger, my mother said in 1979, is the only one that improves by being examined; every finger, she said, is the finger of a glove that has agreed to look like a digit. She said the glove was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 手指（指那只手上每一根旁边的那一根）
B. n. 手指（指那一根本身，与手掌相对）
C. 固定搭配：bandage a finger 包扎一根手指
D. n. 手指（指留给戒指的那一根）
E. n. 手指（抽象总称，指一间病房的包扎之事）
F. n. 手指（指计划里写到、被检查过的那一根）
G. n. （手套的）指部；指状物（指一件事里人人都等却无人检查的那样东西）
H. n. 指状物（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人检查的那样东西）

items.q: bandaged a finger that no doctor in the ward would have examined
The finger, meaning the digit itself and not the hand
the finger at the far side
the finger was the whole of the matter
The finger, meaning the finger of the glove
the finger had become a line in a plan
The finger of the whole thing
A finger, my mother said in 1979

answers.why: bandage a finger 意为“包扎一根手指”，1968 年那位护士包扎了一根病房里没有一位医生肯检查的手指。
finger 意为“手指”，指那一根本身而不是手掌，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被检查。
finger 意为“手指”，指那只手上每一根旁边的那一根，每一根旁边都有同一条短短的绷带。
finger 意为“手指”，指留给戒指的那一根，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
finger 意为“手套的指部、指状物”，指一件事里人人都等却无人检查的那样东西，叔叔说手套的那一指就是那件事的全部。
finger 意为“指状物”，指人人都等却无人检查的那样东西而不是那一根手指，是事情里人人都等、却无人检查的东西。
finger 意为“手指”，指计划里写到、被检查过的那一根，到 1975 年这一根成了计划里的一行。
finger 意为“手指”，护士七月写道，整件事的包扎之事是一间病房和三个星期的检查。
finger 意为“手指”，我记得的是计划里检查过的那一根，1977 年结束了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一根。
finger 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，一根手指是唯一会因为被好好检查而变得更好的东西。
